label: Description of Accident
text: I had parked outside my sister's house on Willow Street and gone inside to collect a box. When I came back out the front nearside of my car was pushed in and there was a silver saloon stopped further up the road. My car was parked at the kerb and nobody was in it.

label: Recorded statement of Dana Whitfield
text:
[00:00:12] ADJUSTER: Can you take me through what happened on the fourteenth?
[00:00:18] MS WHITFIELD: I'd been at my sister's on Willow Street. I left there and I was heading north, back towards the junction.
[00:00:31] ADJUSTER: And roughly what speed were you doing?
[00:00:34] MS WHITFIELD: Twenty, twenty-five. It is a narrow road, you cannot do much more.
[00:00:41] ADJUSTER: So you were stopped at the light when the other vehicle hit you, is that right?
[00:00:47] MS WHITFIELD: No, I was still moving. I had not got to the lights yet.
[00:00:53] ADJUSTER: What time would this have been?
[00:00:56] MS WHITFIELD: That evening, after I had my tea. I could not tell you exactly.
[00:01:04] ADJUSTER: And you reported it to us on the twentieth?
[00:01:08] MS WHITFIELD: That is right. I wanted to see if the other driver would sort it first.

label: Written account of Elaine Torrance
text: I was in my front room at number 41 when I heard the bang. I came out and there was a dark blue hatchback across the middle of the road with its front end damaged, and a silver car further up with its hazards on. The road was wet; it had been raining on and off all day. I did not see the collision itself, only what was there afterwards.
